items.text: Reading all of ~/.codex would make a transcript source an ambient-authority reader and risk exposing credentials. Making it a native adapter would put Codex's evolving record format in the daemon core. Using the live Codex integration to acquire history would conflate lifecycle glue with archival acquisition.
path: ADR-045: Codex history is an installed WebAssembly source

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Codex can change its JSONL schema without destabilising the daemon: unsupported lines are skipped. The source may need updating when Codex changes the session path or the useful record shapes. The release bundles it like Pi and OpenCode, so it is installed from the start and only needs enabling.
path: ADR-045: Codex history is an installed WebAssembly source

items.title: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted. Builds on ADR-024, ADR-025 and ADR-032.
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: Context
items.text: Validity dates and drawer supersession preserve when knowledge was claimed, but cannot say why two independent sources disagree, or why a person corrected one assertion. Similar drawer text does not establish either truth or contradiction. The original drawers must remain evidence even when a graph assertion is no longer believed.
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: Decision
items.text:
flowchart LR
    D1[Evidence drawer A] --> F1[Graph assertion A]
    D2[Evidence drawer B] --> F2[Graph assertion B]
    F2 -->|fact_link: confirms / contradicts / supersedes / refines| F1
    F1 -->|valid_from, valid_to| Time[Validity interval]
    F2 -->|valid_from, valid_to| Time

The relates_to edge is the assertion; the fact_link table holds immutable decisions connecting assertion IDs. Each link records its kind, origin (inferred or explicit), reason, recorded instant and an evidence-drawer ID when available. Direct checkpoint assertions point to the checkpoint drawer through assertion; extracted edges retain their existing drawer/job/extractor provenance. Lifecycle state is computed from these records on read rather than stored as a mutable status column. Schema is applied by SurrealKit and no legacy claims are guessed or merged during migration.

After resolving entities, extraction confirms claims with equal subject, predicate and object and overlapping validity from independent evidence. When a source drawer replaces an earlier version, resolved facts with the same subject and predicate are also linked as supersedes to the closed assertions from that predecessor drawer. This uses explicit drawer lineage rather than assuming that two independently mined documents are revisions. It identifies different objects as contradictory only when the normalized predicate is located_in, interpreted by this first policy as one primary location; other predicates (works_on, uses, member_of, and so on) are multi-valued. Free-text assertions are not automatically assigned a predicate's cardinality. An inferred disagreement leaves both edges open and visible with conflicting state; it never chooses truth from recency. For presentation only, an unresolved conflict's preferred ID is ranked by direct assertion, then confidence, valid_from, then ID, and basis describes the tie breaks. This hint does not remove or invalidate other evidence. The rule and its version are recorded in each inferred link's reason, not obtained from a provider-specific extractor.

An explicit checkpoint supersession atomically closes the targeted edge, opens its replacement and links the two. An explicit invalidation closes an edge without replacement and records its reason. A caller may explicitly link two existing assertions as confirms, contradicts or refines with a nonblank reason; refinement is not inferred from text similarity. Deterministic link IDs make retries safe, and fact IDs derived from the checkpoint item or extracted drawer preserve the same identity across a replay. Inferred links never override an explicit correction.

An assertion's validity uses the existing half-open [valid_from, valid_to) interval. An as_of read ignores explicit decisions recorded after its requested instant and judges conflicts only against other claims valid at that instant; inferred comparisons remain visible when their evidence was discovered later. Current graph and graph expansion omit closed edges but include both sides of unresolved conflicts. Drawer search still returns verbatim evidence under its own temporal filter; an assertion link never rewrites a drawer. GET /api/relationships/{id}/history, memcastle_fact_history and memcastle fact history expose the decision trail.
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: Alternatives rejected
items.text: Automatically superseding a disagreeing claim by arrival time would mistake later extraction for a correction and erase the visible disagreement. Inferring conflicts for every different object would treat multi-valued facts such as uses as mutually exclusive. Asking an LLM to arbitrate every claim would make replay dependent on a provider and would hide the policy behind a model. Storing a mutable current flag on every edge would duplicate validity and link state and could diverge after a crash.
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Corrections preserve their predecessor's content and provenance, and conflicting sources can coexist without silent overwriting. There is no general-purpose truth maintenance: a claim outside the conservative cardinality rule remains open until someone explicitly relates or corrects it.
path: ADR-046: Fact lifecycle is an auditable relation between assertions

items.title: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls
path: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted.
path: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls

items.title: Context
items.text: The web dashboard already reads identifier-only change notices from GET /api/events and fetches authoritative state from REST. Operators also need a full-screen terminal view of mining jobs, readiness and maintenance without moving business logic into a CLI process. Unlike cooperative cancellation, a force-cancel may stop a local worker before it checkpoints; an interrupted request must remain durable across a daemon restart, and a different daemon's lease must never be overwritten.
path: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls

items.title: Decision
items.text:
memcastle tui uses ratatui and crossterm for rendering and input, and client::DaemonClient for every daemon call. Its Rust SSE reader uses the web dashboard's existing authenticated endpoint and wire format, never a parallel bus. Events prompt rereads; reconnect, resync, a manual refresh and periodic reconciliation cover gaps in that process-local stream.

The REST-only POST /api/jobs/{id}/force-cancel applies to a locally owned running mining job. The scheduler first persists cancel_requested, then aborts and joins its task. It applies JobEvent::Cancel through Job::apply and checks running status and lease owner atomically before answering. A crash between those steps is recovered as a cancellation, and subsequent fenced writes from the old run are refused. Blocking work outside the task may continue briefly and previously filed data remains filed; force-cancel does not claim process isolation or instant termination. The ordinary pause and cancel routes remain cooperative, preserving checkpoint-friendly behavior.
path: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls

items.title: Consequences
items.text: The terminal and browser share one domain and event model, while each keeps its own presentation and stream reader. No new storage, credential handling, MCP control or event replay is needed. An owner on a different daemon cannot be force-cancelled through this daemon; the caller receives a rejection and can ask for graceful cancellation instead.
path: ADR-047: Terminal operations console shares daemon events and controls

items.title: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides
path: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted.
path: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides

items.title: Context
items.text: Mined drawers have an adapter name and source-document metadata, but retrieval used relevance alone and conflict presentation used explicitness, confidence and validity time without source authority. One daemon serves one palace; the global XDG configuration is not copied with palace data.
path: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Use three ordered levels (low, normal, high) rather than expose numeric tuning. The global configuration declares [preferences], the same file can override it under [palace.preferences], and a preferences-only <palace.path>/preferences.toml can override both. Merge individual fields, and replace a connector's criteria only when explicitly supplied; criteria = [] clears them. An absent preference defaults to normal, and an unknown adapter name is permitted as a future connector. Matching criteria compare JSON scalar values at connector-specific dot-separated metadata paths, without imposing a shared schema on source authors. More-specific paths win, with declaration order deciding equal-depth matches. The matching document metadata is snapshotted with a mined drawer's origin so later revisions cannot retroactively change historical evidence; a change to the policy itself is evaluated at read time.

flowchart LR
  Global[Global preferences] --> Merge[Field-wise merge]
  Palace[Global palace overrides] --> Merge
  Local[Palace preferences.toml] --> Merge
  Merge --> Policy[Effective preference policy]
  Origin[Drawer origin and metadata] --> Resolve[Resolve connector and criterion]
  Policy --> Resolve
  Resolve --> Extract[Extraction context]
  Resolve --> Conflict[Conflict presentation]
  Resolve --> Search[Scoped candidate reranking]

The ranking adjustment is bounded and applies only to already relevant, temporally eligible candidates. Search normalizes relevance inside the candidate pool and adjusts it by at most 0.08 for either extreme; the original BM25, cosine or fusion signal remains visible alongside the effective preference on a search hit. Graph expansion remains after direct search results. For unresolved conflicts, explicit assertions precede the read-side hint; confidence, bounded freshness and a smaller source adjustment decide between other open facts, without closing either assertion. Supersession and temporal validity determine eligibility before any preference calculation. Extraction passes the preference and provenance context to command and HTTP providers, but preserves provider confidence and the configured extraction floor; source priority does not make a claim true. Exact/near deduplication keeps independent mined evidence rather than merging sources into a single authority. The server does not generate answers: search, recall and fact responses carry provenance and preference explanations for clients that synthesize answers from evidence.
path: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Adding a connector needs no MemCastle code change to the policy; only its metadata conventions need documenting. Changing configuration requires a daemon restart, while old provenance and contradictory evidence remain inspectable. Future query-specific strategies can use the same effective policy without changing the TOML contract.
path: ADR 048: Source preference is bounded evidence, with palace-local overrides

items.title: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases
items.text: Status: Accepted
path: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases

items.title: Context
items.text: ADR-026 runs a single source WASM component behind SourceAdapter, ADR-033 distributes one source package per registry entry, and ADR-034 installs an agent integration from the Core assets root. None is a unit of release for an upstream provider that supplies several sources and an agent integration. Coupling every upstream compatibility fix to a Core version prevents independent provider CI and releases.
path: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases

items.title: Decision
items.text:
One standalone provider repository publishes one versioned plugin archive with a root plugin.toml. During the in-tree transition, multiple provider directories under plugins/ use independent version tags and explicit catalogue asset URLs instead of treating the Core repository as a direct one-plugin discovery URL. The manifest owns stable plugin and module IDs, compatibility, dependencies, checked artifact paths and per-module types. Module-specific source and integration manifests remain authoritative for their own runtime contract and permissions. The plugin catalogue at plugins.json is reviewed discovery metadata with a module inventory, not a safety endorsement; the existing registry.json remains an unchanged format-1 source catalogue.

The daemon verifies an indexed or GitHub-reported release digest before reading its archive, checks the manifest against catalogue metadata, and applies the configured plugin signature policy. A direct GitHub repository URL and a local built project/archive are also explicit installation inputs. The install stages an immutable generation and transactionally publishes package ownership and source module records. Source ownership and live module IDs are checked in that transaction, so competing installations cannot take over a cursor or make an integration ID ambiguous after preflight. Adding a module leaves it inactive; upgrading keeps the existing source module's state and credential agreement unless its permissions change. Removing or changing the type of a module requires disabling it and removing configured miners or agent registrations. Uninstall refuses dependents, active jobs, configured miners and enabled sources. It deletes installation records and credentials, never mined drawers, source documents or their cursors. The local pointer is hidden before database publication and restored on rollback, so local integrations never point to a retired generation after a successful transaction. Credential cleanup follows publication; startup retries interrupted cleanup from retained source ownership and removes pointers whose plugin ledger entry is gone.

Source modules continue through ADR-026's WASM host and the unchanged mining pipeline. Agent integrations continue to be installed locally by the CLI, from a selected installed plugin generation; there is no route or MCP tool that registers an integration in an agent. embedding_provider has a separate versioned Wasm runtime contract and profile selection in ADR-051.

GitTPL templates live in three independent repositories. The parent template composes source and integration templates repeatedly from recorded module IDs and locks resolved commits, allowing the same generated project to run under plugins/<provider>/ or in a standalone repository. Core and provider CI/release workflows select their own changed paths and independent version tags.
path: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases

items.title: Consequences
items.text: An old source package remains available through the legacy REST/CLI commands without a data rewrite; it cannot be silently claimed by a new plugin of the same source name. A removed legacy source with mined history needs --adopt-source <id> to make the handoff explicit. An uninstalled plugin keeps the source-ID ownership marker so another publisher cannot inherit its preserved cursor. The package is the unit of download and trust, while enablement, configured miner scope, integration registration and source cursor remain independent. GitTPL 0.14 records the commit resolved from each child main branch on init and update; advancing the rendered ref remains explicit, and the author takes its changes with a normal Git merge.
path: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: A plugin per source kind would duplicate provider authentication and force Jira and Confluence into different releases. Reinterpreting registry.json as a plugin index would break format-1 clients and their published digests. Making integrations implement SourceAdapter would give agent-side lifecycle code permissions it does not need.
path: ADR-049: Provider plugins are distributed as multi-module releases

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted.

items.title: Context
items.text: An embedding is derived from canonical drawer content, an input pipeline, a model, and a provider connection. Two 768-dimensional vectors from different models are no more comparable than vectors of different lengths. The original drawer.embedding field and HNSW index record none of that information.

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Named embedding profiles select a named provider connection, model, and dimension. A non-secret fingerprint includes the connection identity, provider protocol, model, dimension, input truncation length, and pipeline version; credential material is never stored in jobs or vectors. One derived drawer_embedding record per drawer and fingerprint holds the vector, the original content hash, the hash of the actual provider input, and the full non-secret provenance. The selected profile and fingerprint are pinned in durable jobs. On resume, a missing or changed connection fails the job instead of silently changing its vector space. Automatic jobs fill only missing vectors; explicitly requested stale and all refreshes may replace derived records.

The old field's vectors are retained as unknown provenance, not assigned to a default profile or read by profile search. SurrealKit's version-4 destructive rollout retires the old HNSW index while keeping its field's values. The embedding-quarantine data-migration watermark records that transition; re-embedding is a separately requested, resumable job and never happens during database migration. Canonical content, graph links and temporal validity do not depend on derived vectors. Supported writes never edit a drawer's content in place: a correction closes the old drawer and files a new one. Its existing vector stays with the old drawer for historical searches, while current semantic search ignores it until the replacement has its own embedding; a concurrent embedding write also checks the content hash before storing. Direct database-admin edits to canonical content bypass this contract and require a deliberate refresh/recovery.

SurrealDB HNSW indexes have fixed dimensions and an index cannot contain two incompatible spaces merely because they have the same dimension. The profile-filtered exact-search path works for arbitrary positive dimensions, applying the selected fingerprint and drawer scope inside the database before ranking or limiting. Schema-declared 768/1536/3072 projection tables provide dedicated index tiers; a tier can only be assigned to one immutable space at a time. Other spaces of the same dimension use exact ranking instead of sharing its HNSW index. Each tier has one slot for the lifetime of the palace: the first embedding written at that dimension claims it, even if its profile is later disabled or removed. There is no automatic promotion of another profile into the slot, and exact ranking scans the matching space's vectors, so its cost grows with that profile's corpus size. An operator who needs a particular profile indexed must choose it before the first embedding at that dimension; multiple large profiles of one dimension may warrant additional bounded, schema-declared slots in a later decision. No vector from a provenance-free drawer is eligible for any profile-aware semantic result.

The configured model identifier is part of the fingerprint, but Core cannot observe a provider silently changing the weights behind an unchanged alias at the same endpoint. Prefer a provider's immutable version or digest as the configured model identifier when it accepts one. If the provider exposes only a mutable alias, pin its revision in the provider's own deployment and deliberately change the profile/model setting (then re-embed) when that alias is repointed; otherwise provenance records the requested identifier, not an independently verified model revision.

items.title: Alternatives rejected
items.text: Reusing the drawer's single HNSW index for every 768-dimensional model was rejected because length alone cannot establish compatibility, and a dimension-filtered search would still leave incompatible vectors in the same physical index. Creating arbitrary indexes at runtime was rejected because MemCastle delegates all schema definitions to SurrealKit; dynamic profile names and arbitrary vector lengths cannot safely generate schema DDL in application code. Discarding all legacy vectors during migration was rejected because their contents may still be useful for manual recovery.

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Changing a profile's model or endpoint creates a new space, so old vectors remain recoverable but cannot be searched under the new configuration until an explicit re-embedding job populates it. Exact ranking is slower for large palaces than a dedicated HNSW index, but never compares incompatible vectors. Caller-supplied vectors need an explicit configured profile, including when the connection is external and the daemon has no embedding provider of its own.

items.title: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted.
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: Context
items.text: A plugin can distribute sources and agent integrations, but neither contract can produce query or drawer embeddings. Named connections and profiles already define selection and provenance (ADR-050); the plugin catalogue already carries an embedding_provider inventory (ADR-049). An executable module needs its own compatibility contract and isolation without making an OpenAI-compatible endpoint depend on an OpenAI product plugin.
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: Decision
items.text:
An embedding_provider module supplies memcastle-embedding.toml and a wasm32-wasip2 embedding.wasm component implementing memcastle:embedding@0.1.0. Its own manifest declares the module ID, version, contract, supported model IDs and dimensions, an optional restricted JSON schema for non-secret settings, and whether it needs network and host-scoped credential access. The parent plugin manifest names and hashes those files and agrees on the module's identity, schema and contract. The daemon checks the component's declared models against its actual models export before making it selectable. The component receives ordered text batches, selected model, dimension and validated settings; the host verifies vector count, dimension and finite coordinates.

The Wasm host provides no files, environment, arguments or process execution. Network is granted only when declared in the module manifest and expressly consented to during plugin install; a credential is available only from the selected connection's env or file reference during an embedding call, and only when that module declared access. The permission digest is per embedding module, separate from source consents; a changed permission set requires new consent. Credentials and their contents are excluded from module manifests, plugin records, job payloads and embedding spaces.

An [embeddings.providers.NAME] connection with type = "plugin" selects an installed plugin ID and embedding module ID. Its ordinary [embeddings.profiles.NAME] supplies the model and dimensions, so default, miner override, explicit job and search selection share the same precedence and validation as Core providers. The daemon starts with an unavailable plugin-backed profile; attempting to select it reports the missing installation while other profiles continue to work. Successful installation refreshes the scheduler's and search's common provider registry without a restart. Uninstall is refused while a profile or active pinned job references that plugin; updates removing referenced modules or replacing bytes used by an active pinned job are refused.

A plugin-backed embedding space fingerprints the non-secret connection settings, plugin and module identities, module version and component digest along with ADR-050's model, dimension and pipeline identity. A changed implementation therefore gets a new space rather than reusing old vectors; a resumed job refuses to cross spaces. Core's command and OpenAI-compatible HTTP implementations remain available without a plugin, including OpenRouter and other compatible servers.
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: Alternatives rejected
items.text: Treating a source miner or chat integration as an embedding provider was rejected because neither contract advertises a vector model, its dimensions or a compatible embedding space. Running plugin binaries directly was rejected in favour of the existing component isolation model: an executable can inherit ambient files, environment and credentials without an install-time permission grant. A second provider registry was rejected because the plugin archive is already the reviewed, versioned distribution unit.
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Plugin installation and updates use the existing versioned plugin registry, checksums, ownership ledger and generation directories. Providers can ship sources or integrations in the same archive without enabling those modules just to embed text. An incompatible update requires finishing or canceling pinned jobs; existing vectors remain in their original space until the operator requests re-embedding.
path: ADR-051: Embedding provider modules are independently selected Wasm capabilities

items.title: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections
path: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections

items.title: Status
items.text: Accepted.
path: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections

items.title: Context
items.text: An OpenAI or OpenRouter account can serve more than one capability and more than one endpoint. Embedding connections currently hold their own credentials, while source OAuth sign-ins are scoped to source installations. Sharing a source session or copying keys into each embedding profile would conflate distinct lifecycles.
path: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections

items.title: Decision
items.text:
Core defines named [provider_accounts.ID] entries with a provider identity and a generic authentication mechanism. An account references an existing daemon environment variable or owner-controlled file, never an inline secret. Core supports bearer and api_key authentication; the latter has an optional public HTTP header name. An embedding connection selects an account by ID and declares the same provider identity separately from its protocol, endpoint, module and settings. Several connections can select the same account, while several accounts for one provider remain distinct. Future LLM connections can use the same account contract and resolver without introducing an LLM subsystem here.

Credentials are resolved by the daemon at use time, allowing rotation without restarting the server. The HTTP provider sends a token in the selected header. The Wasm host binds only the selected account to one embedding component and serves it only during an embedding call, when that module declared credential access and installation was consented to. The host never supplies the account registry, daemon environment, filesystem or a token during module discovery. The settings API reports account IDs, provider IDs, auth kinds, availability and embedding connection linkage, but never a credential location or value.

Source-specific OAuth grants remain tied to their source and manifest permissions. Product-specific interactive or web-session sign-ins require a separate, explicit provider/integration authentication implementation that defines its renewal and capability contracts; a chat sign-in never implies embedding access. The existing source credential store is not a generic, named provider-token store. Old inline embedding keys/references and legacy single-provider settings continue to work; accounts are opt-in.

Account IDs, credential references, tokens and availability never contribute to embedding-space provenance. Legacy HTTP URLs containing userinfo are fingerprinted without their user/password, so rotating them cannot change a space. Endpoint, provider identity/protocol, non-secret plugin configuration and version, model and dimensions still distinguish vector spaces under ADR-050 and ADR-051. Removing the old plugin credential-reference hash changes the fingerprint of existing plugin profiles once; their previous vectors remain in their old space and need deliberate re-embedding.
path: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections

items.title: Consequences
items.text: Editing provider accounts requires editing the daemon configuration and restarting to change the selected account or credential reference. The secret behind an existing reference may be rotated without restarting. Missing credentials fail the selected request with a redacted, actionable error; unrelated accounts and profiles keep working.
path: ADR-052: Provider accounts are independent of capability connections
